title: Profile generator connector shims for heterogeneous dataset/prompt formats and eval-runner introspection
creator: Priya Nair
description: Overview: We need a lightweight, pluggable set of connector shims and an eval-runner introspection API to make the profile-generator resilient to diverse dataset and prompt formats encountered during model onboarding. Motivation: model onboarding often stalls because dataset ingestion or prompt layout mismatches yield silently incorrect evals or non-representative profiles. The generator should produce canonical performance profiles (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, memory, batching characteristics, cost-per-token estimate) regardless of input format, and should emit metadata that makes version-pinning and rollout decisions reliable. Goals: 1) Implement adapter shims that normalize datasets (JSONL, TSV, HF datasets, zipped archives) into a small canonical record format the harness understands. 2) Provide prompt normalization (placeholder expansion, role-splitting for chat-style prompts, function-calling stubs) so prompts are evaluated consistently across model variants. 3) Add an eval-runner introspection endpoint so runner implementations can declare runtime capabilities and constraints (max_batch_size, supports_streaming, kv_cache_aware, preferred_kernel, deterministic_seeding). 4) Extend profile publishing schema to include runner_capabilities and format_compatibility fields used by the routing layer when doing pinning and fallback. Non-goals: this ticket does not implement full hf dataset ingestion or long-term storage; it focuses on canonicalization and metadata emission. Approach: - Create connectors: jsonl_adapter, tsv_adapter, hf_adapter (thin wrapper that downloads and yields records), zip_adapter. Each adapter must emit: {record_id, prompt_template, input_tokens_estimate, metadata_tags} in the canonical line. - Prompt normalizer: transform role-based chat into tokenized prompt with clear prefix/suffix markers so KV-cache and batching are comparable across models. Support function-call placeholders by replacing with a deterministic sentinel. - Introspection API: runners implement /introspect that returns a consistent JSON blob (stringified here in docs) listing capabilities. The harness will call introspect at the start of a profile job; missing keys fall back to conservative defaults. - Profile schema changes: add fields runner_capabilities (list), format_compatibility (list), sample_token_distribution (string reference to sanitized histogram), and deterministic_seed_used (boolean). Acceptance criteria: - End-to-end profile generation succeeds for 3 canonical datasets (SQuAD-like JSONL, HF classification splits, TSV conversational pairs) without manual per-dataset config. - Published profile JSON validates against the updated schema and includes runner_capabilities and format_compatibility. - CI covers adapters with small sample fixtures; downstream router uses runner_capabilities in a canary rollout test. - No regression in existing benchmark runs (compare against baseline job IDs). Testing plan: unit tests for each adapter, integration test that runs the generator against a small HF dataset (via a stubbed downloader), and an infra test where introspect response is mocked with varying capabilities to ensure fallback logic works. Rollout: land adapter shims behind a feature flag in profile-generator; enable for internal model-onboarding jobs first, then enable for all onboarding by default in two iterations. Metrics & observability: track % of onboarding profiles that required manual dataset overrides, time-to-generate profile, and downstream routing mismatches caused by missing runner metadata. Risks: adapters could inadvertently mutate prompts (mitigated by strict normalization tests), introspect adds extra RPCs (cached per-runner), differing tokenizers across models require we record tokenizer_id in profile metadata. References: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Profile+Generator+Connector+Shims GitHub draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness/pull/4682 Internal experiment dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/bench/profile-generation-experiments
